Islamorada flats fishing: bonefish, permit and trip choice

Plan an Islamorada flats trip with clear bonefish and permit choices, seasonal context, a skiff packing list and official license links.

Source-checked · Updated 10 November 2026 · Castward editorial

Who this trip suits

Choose this trip if you want a focused shallow-water day and accept that the guide may spend time looking for fish. Tell the guide whether you want to learn to cast, try a new species, or maximize time with a familiar method.

For a first outing, ask about seated rest breaks, shade and instruction. A sight-fishing skiff day can require patience and accurate casts. A party that wants everyone to fish continuously should compare the actual boat layout and fishing rotation before paying.

When to go

Use the broad bonefish window as an initial travel filter. FWC’s species page describes a March–October peak; the county guide highlights fall. Neither source ranks individual weeks at Islamorada.

Ask the guide to explain the tide, wind and visibility for your dates. Request a second fishing plan before you commit. The permit rule calendar is a legal check, not a measure of catch probability.

Source: FWC: bonefish · FWC: where to saltwater fish — Monroe County · FWC: permit regulations · NWS: Florida Keys marine forecasts

How to arrange the day

Confirm the actual Islamorada meeting marina before you choose accommodation. A listing for the Florida Keys can refer to a different island or departure. Save the dock name, map pin, parking instructions and a direct contact number.

Agree whether the trip stays in the skiff. Wading is a separate decision that needs permission, local conditions and suitable footwear. Do not pack chest waders merely because the trip involves shallow water. Ask who makes the weather decision and when you will receive it.

What the guide provides: confirm each item

No guide inventory is verified here. Ask for a written list of rods, reels, leaders, flies or bait, landing equipment and safety equipment. Specify a left- or right-handed reel preference when relevant.

Also confirm passenger capacity, storage, shade, toilet arrangements and the plan for children or mobility needs. Mark “Guide provides” in the planner only for the items the operator names. A saltwater charter license is a separate question from a captain’s credential.

Source: FWC: saltwater charter license coverage

Local mistakes to avoid

  • Treating bonefish and permit as interchangeable targets with one guaranteed season.
  • Booking an offshore permit opportunity while expecting a shallow flats day.
  • Arriving at a different Keys marina because the island was not specified.
  • Assuming every flat allows fishing or that a nearby protected zone has the same rules.
  • Buying a full fly outfit before the guide confirms the method and provision.

Regulations and licenses

Start with the FWC visitor license page. Ask whether the exact for-hire vessel has valid saltwater charter coverage. Check bonefish and permit rules, including the Special Permit Zone, for your trip date.

Use NOAA’s sanctuary guidance for the planned area. State, federal and sanctuary rules can overlap. Follow the live authority pages for fees, limits, handling requirements and closures; this guide does not reproduce them as fixed facts.

Source: FWC: visitor licenses · FWC: bonefish · FWC: permit regulations · NOAA: Florida Keys sanctuary fishing regulations

Questions and answers

Is fly fishing required for an Islamorada flats trip?

No single method is assumed here. Ask the guide which fly or spinning option fits the target, your skill and the conditions.

What is the best time for bonefish in Islamorada?

FWC gives March–October as a broad Keys peak, while its county guide highlights fall. Choose the actual day with local tide, wind and visibility information.

Does the charter cover my Florida license?

It can if the for-hire vessel has valid Florida saltwater charter coverage. Confirm that coverage with the operator and check FWC’s visitor rules.
